name: The Sacred Char Dham
description: The four sacred abodes established by Adi Shankaracharya in Uttarakhand, believed to open the doors of Moksha.

sites.name: Yamunotri Dham
sites.importance: Westernmost Dham, origin of River Yamuna from Champasar Glacier.

sites.name: Gangotri Dham
sites.importance: Sacred seat where Ganga descended upon Lord Shiva's matted locks.

sites.name: Kedarnath Dham
sites.importance: One of the 12 Jyotirlingas, where Shiva manifested as a hump to Pandavas.

sites.name: Badrinath Dham
sites.importance: One of India's major Char Dham and Chota Char Dham, abode of Lord Vishnu.

name: The Holy Panch Prayag
description: The five sacred river confluences of the Alaknanda river cascading down from the Himalayas to form the holy Ganges.

sites.name: Vishnuprayag
sites.importance: First confluence where Sage Narada meditated to please Lord Vishnu.

sites.name: Nandaprayag
sites.importance: King Nanda performed yagna here; holy site of purification.

sites.name: Karnaprayag
sites.importance: Karna worshipped Sun God Surya and received divine Kavach and Kundal here.

sites.name: Rudraprayag
sites.importance: Lord Shiva performed the Rudra Tandava and blessed Sage Narada with music mastery.

sites.name: Devprayag
sites.importance: The ultimate confluence where River Ganga officially begins its pilgrimage across India.

name: The Divine Panch Kedar
description: The five Shiva temples built by the Pandavas in the Garhwal Himalayas where different parts of Lord Shiva's bull incarnation appeared.
